title: Expose X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Verified in NNTP ARTICLE response
description:
What: When serving ARTICLE (and HEAD) responses, if did_sig_valid is Some in the OverviewRecord, add X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Verified: true|false header to the response.

Algorithm:
1. Find the ARTICLE/HEAD command handler in crates/reader/src/session/ (likely commands/article.rs or handlers/article.rs)
2. When retrieving the article to serve, also look up the OverviewRecord via overview_store.query_by_msgid() or similar to get did_sig_valid
3. If did_sig_valid is Some(true): inject header 'X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Verified: true' into the response headers before the blank line
4. If did_sig_valid is Some(false): inject header 'X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Verified: false'
5. If did_sig_valid is None: do not add the header (absent = no DID sig was present)
6. Advertise X-USENET-IPFS-DID-VERIFIED in CAPABILITIES response (find where capabilities are listed and add it)

Defensive programming:
- Header injection must not break RFC 5322 header format
- Only add header if overview lookup succeeds — on lookup failure, silently omit rather than failing the ARTICLE command
- The X- prefix marks this as an extension; standard clients will ignore it per RFC 3977 §3.3
- Log at debug level if header injection happens, not info
